1.why: Text is a clean sans-serif with reasonable letter and line spacing and clear label/field separation across all eight screens.

2.why: No italics or all-caps are used and body copy is short, though the growing stack of eight identical red banners becomes a dense mass of text by step 8.

3.why: Content is laid out in a single narrow column with full-width fields and button, which reads well at mobile width.

4.why: Instructions such as 'Sign in to start your security setup.' and 'Use your saved password' are one short line in plain language.

5.why: 'Example: marcus@example.com' is shown under the email field and a demo credential hint is given in the info box.

6.why: Although the base copy is short, by later screens the user must wade through six to eight repeated identical error banners before reaching the form.

7.why: No secret, OTP or recovery code screen is ever reached, so no copy-to-clipboard affordance is observable in any screenshot.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry appears anywhere in the eight screenshots.

9.why: The email and password fields appear pre-populated with saved credentials and the hint 'Use your saved password' indicates autofill/password-manager support.

10.why: A prominent blue 'Sign in' button is clear, but the step indicator 'Step 1 of 4' is small, low-contrast, and never changes despite repeated attempts.

11.why: Each screen asks for only one main action — completing the sign-in form and pressing the single primary 'Sign in' button.

12.why: After every submission the system only repeats the same vague failure banner, never stating what actually happened or what comes next, and the Logs panel is empty.

13.why: The user can retry sign-in repeatedly with no lockout shown, but no reveal/hide or re-request code functions are reachable to evaluate.

14.why: 'Check your email and password, then try again.' is non-blaming but generic — it names neither the specific problem nor a concrete fix, and it is duplicated eight times.

15.why: No countdown timers, expiry warnings, or auto-advancing elements appear on any screen, so reading is untimed.
